newsitem.title: MEXICO: Results show opposition grabs Mexico capital.
newsitem.headline: Results show opposition grabs Mexico capital.

text.p: Opposition leader Cuauhtemoc Cardenas took almost twice as many votes as his nearest rival in last Sunday's race for mayor of Mexico City, official results released late on Friday said.

Cardenas, running for the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), won 1,859,866 votes, or 47.11 percent of the vote, official results from the local wing of the Federal Electoral Institute show.
His nearest rival, Alfredo del Mazo, of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) gained 990,306 votes, or 25.08 percent of the total.
Carlos Castillo Peraza of the right-wing National Action Party (PAN) took 602,466 votes, or 15.26 percent.
Other smaller parties also took a portion of the vote.

The vote on Sunday was the first for a mayor in Mexico City in decades. The cabinet level post had been filled by the president of the republic, assuring the post would remain with the PRI, which has ruled Mexico for the last 68 years.
As well as delivering the mayor's job of one of the world's largest cities to the opposition, voters also stripped the PRI of its majority in the lower house of Congress in the July 6 vote.
The son of one of Mexico's former presidents, Lazaro Cardenas, Cuauhtemoc Cardenas had suffered defeats in the last two elections when he ran for president of the nation.
Many Mexicans believe he was cheated of victory in 1988 by fraud, but in 1994, after a lackluster campaign, he lost in an election generally regarded as clean.
The PRD also won a lion's share of the seats in the assembly in the federal district, the nation's capital, in last Sunday's vote, results showed.
